chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Zayyat, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A woman saw blood during her menstruation until it went beyond its time; when should she perform salat (prayer)?

He said: "She considers the number of days she used to refrain, then she exercises precaution up to ten days. If she sees the blood as flowing blood, then she should perform ghusl at the time of every salat (prayer)."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his statement "by ten days" is "up to ten days," and particles of qualification may stand in place of one another, because we have already explained that precautionary waiting is only for one day, or two days, or three. So when it reaches ten days, that is the maximum number of days of menstruation, and there is no precautionary waiting after that.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she observes precautionary waiting beyond her habitual period
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the maximum limit discussed here for menstruation
key_terms.فَلْتَغْتَسِلْ: then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.وَقْتُهَا: its usual appointed time or duration

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if menstrual bleeding continues beyond her usual days in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman whose bleeding continues beyond her usual menstrual period. It explains that she should consider her habitual days, observe precaution within the limit of ten days, and after that limit the ruling changes, with Shaykh al-Tusi clarifying that ten days is the maximum period of hayd.
